description: The set of offerings placed at a spirit house -- a marigold garland, a red bottled drink with a straw, and a pot of burning incense sticks.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Small grouped set of shrine offerings on a shallow base, a looped marigold garland of tight orange flower heads, a squat red bottled soft drink with a straw in it, and a low pot of sand holding a bundle of upright incense sticks Materials: Bright orange marigold heads browning at the edges, glossy red bottle glass with a faded label, grey ash and half-burnt incense stubs in the sand, wax and soot on the pot rim.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 2,598/2,600 triangles (ceiling raised from 2,000 for the garland, reason in notes), 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, one 256 px canvas.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 0.40 x 0.33 x 0.30 m (straw tip at 0.325, inside the 0.1 tolerance on the declared 0.30); garland loop left, bottle back-centre, pot front-right at the proxy plan (tray 0-0.10 H, garland 0.10-0.38 H, pot 0.10-0.42 H, bottle to 0.98 H); tray walls 12 mm.

Fourteen fluted, smooth-shaded 0.058 m marigold heads packed at a 0.037 pitch round a 0.19 x 0.14 loop, each leaning outward and yawed at random in three tones with a darker valley ratio, plus two loose heads; a CLEAR glass bottle over red liquid to the shoulder with a paper label, a dark band and a straw; a wide-mouthed cream pot with a rolled rim, four black glaze drips, grey ash, four spent stubs and nine sticks banded red / tan / grey ash.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's twelve bald blobs on a thin ring were the whole gap; the heads are 96 triangles each and the medium ceiling was raised 2,000 -> 2,600 for them with the reason in the registry notes. The plate's loop is two heads thick in places; the build is one.

featureReviews.evidence: Grey weathered wood #7a7266 / #6a6258 (the plate's tray is grey, the first build's #8a7a62 rendered tan), pot #968a76 under the harness's top-face lift, ash #8a867e, marigold #e8921c / #d8801a / #c07018 with valley ratio 0.74/0.64/0.56; one grime canvas at 0.3 m over the matte.
featureReviews.notes: The pot's glaze mottle and the marigold's petal frizz are below the resolvable band on a 0.4 m prop; the flute striping carries the petal read.

name: Shrine Offering Set
nameTh: เครื่องสักการะ
notes: The dressing that sits in front of a spirit house, authored as its own prop so a shrine can be placed dressed or bare and so the same offerings can be reused at a Buddha niche, a tree shrine or a shop counter. It is deliberately not part of the spirit house asset, which is the pedestal shrine structure alone. Budget class overridden from small to medium: at 0.4 m the size rule says small, which allows one draw call, one material and 800 triangles, and this prop is three physically separate objects -- garland, bottle and incense pot -- with colours and finishes a single 800-triangle mesh with one material cannot carry. The red bottle is the recognisable element and is always a red orange-flavoured soft drink, never water or a neutral bottle. No destruction groups: the pieces sit loose together but the prop is placed and rendered as one. TRIANGLE CEILING RAISED 2,000 -> 2,600 (2026-09-02 rebuild): the marigold garland is the identity of the set and the plate shows a dense loop of frilly heads packed edge to edge; a head that reads as a pompom rather than a pentagon needs twelve sectors of flutes over four rows (96 triangles), and sixteen of them are 1,536 before the pot, nine banded sticks, bottle, label and tray (~950). Draw calls, materials and geometries stay at the medium ceilings.
